# Test Fixtures — Plan 02-15

Files in this directory are shared by Phase 2 tests (unit, integration, e2e).

## `test-avatar.png`

A minimal, deterministic, valid PNG (8x8 px, single colour) used by the
happy-path photo upload e2e spec. Generated by
`build-test-avatar.ts`. Run once per checkout if missing:

```bash
pnpm tsx tests/fixtures/build-test-avatar.ts
```

The file is checked in for convenience but can be regenerated bit-identical
if it ever drifts.

## `eicar.png` — EICAR test fixture

**WHAT IT IS**

`eicar.png` is a synthetic file whose magic bytes are a valid PNG header but
whose body embeds the **EICAR Standard Anti-Virus Test File** signature —
the industry-standard string used since 1991 to verify that an
anti-malware product is correctly configured.

The EICAR signature is:

```
X5O!P%@AP[4\PZX54(P^)7CC)7}$EICAR-STANDARD-ANTIVIRUS-TEST-FILE!$H+H*
```

Documented at <https://www.eicar.org/download-anti-malware-testfile/>.
The string is **not malicious** — it is a public-domain, well-known
text pattern. Any conforming AV scanner (ClamAV, Sophos, Microsoft
Defender, etc.) recognises it and reports "Eicar-Test-Signature".

**WHY WE USE IT**

Phase 2 introduces a malware-scan pipeline (Plan 02-06 worker, ClamAV
container in production). We need a deterministic positive case to verify:

1. The scan worker actually invokes the AV engine.
2. The `uploaded_files.scan_status` column flips from `pending` to
   `infected`.
3. The UI walks to the `scanInfected` visual state and refuses to serve
   the file via `getSignedUrl`.

Real malware samples are unsafe (and probably illegal) to commit; EICAR
is the only safe option.

**SECURITY POSTURE (T-02-15-FIXTURE-LEAK mitigation)**

The threat register flags this fixture (`T-02-15-FIXTURE-LEAK,
Information Disclosure`). Risk and mitigation:

- **Risk**: a future maintainer mistakes the file for actual malware and
  reports it as a security incident; or an AV scanner installed locally
  flags `git pull` / `git push` and quarantines it.
- **Mitigation**: we **do not commit the raw EICAR bytes**. Instead, the
  `eicar.png` file is **built at test setup time** by
  `build-eicar-png.ts`, which concatenates a PNG header with the EICAR
  string from an in-source constant. Local AV scanners may still detect
  the generated artefact in `tests/fixtures/` — that's expected; either
  whitelist the path or accept the noise.
- **Convention**: do not commit the generated `eicar.png` to git. The
  `.gitignore` rule below enforces this.

```
# .gitignore (project root)
tests/fixtures/eicar.png
```

Run the builder before any test that needs the fixture:

```bash
pnpm tsx tests/fixtures/build-eicar-png.ts
```

The Playwright e2e config can call this script in `globalSetup` once
Plan 02-15 lands; for now invoke manually if running the photo-upload
spec locally.
